fieldNotes.truckGate: Two access points off Oberlin Ave SW funnel into the property: a wide open driveway at ~40.7805,-81.5395 leading south through the campus, and a fenced/gated south-side entry at ~40.7800,-81.5388 with chain-link sliding gate visible in Street View (May 2024). Both serve truck traffic; the south-side fenced entry is clearly the controlled commercial gate.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No clear staffed guard booth resolved in either satellite or Street View. The fenced south entry has bollards and signage but no obvious staffed shack at the lane. Marked uncertain — could be an unmanned kiosk/remote check-in.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: Inferred: gate exists but no shack visible; large frozen-food plant of this scale (~400-700 employees, Smart Ones / Bagel Bites manufacturing) likely uses remote check-in via guard at the main reception or app-based.
fieldNotes.preGateStaging: No clear truck-stall apron outside the gate on Oberlin; tree buffer + grass strip between road and fence.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved open area between the gate and dock faces, particularly the wide central yard between buildings — easily holds 5+ trucks waiting for a dock.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Both access driveways have ~150-200m of internal road before reaching dock faces — plenty of stacking room for 3+ trucks.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Each gate appears to be bidirectional, no separate in/out gates resolved.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Single bidirectional lane at each entry per overhead. Marked uncertain — could be 2 with painted division not resolved.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved gate aprons and unused width at both entries — clear room to add bypass / express lane if appointment system bypassed regular check-in.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Counted across multiple faces: south face of main building ~10-12 doors, SE building face ~10-12 doors, west warehouse south face ~6-8 doors. Total band 25-50 (estimated ~28 visible).
fieldNotes.dropArea: 10-25 trailers visible across the various paved yards. Multiple parked trailers without tractors in the SW dock apron (drop trailers) and a small clustered area east of the docks.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Distinct dock banks on south face (likely shipping outbound) and west/SW face (likely receiving) — physical separation typical of frozen food plants where outbound frozen and inbound packaging/raw goods are handled separately.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Wooded semi-rural setting; small-town industrial fringe of Massillon. Houses to north, fields to south. Per rubric tiebreaker, judged Rural.
fieldNotes.connectivityIssue: Near edge of Massillon city — cellular coverage likely fine; no connectivity issue inferred.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Sprawling campus with 5-6 distinct connected/separate buildings: main processing block, west warehouse (large purple-roof building), SE auxiliary warehouse, and ancillary structures. Multi-building manufacturing campus.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale resolved on satellite. Could exist near south gate but not visible at zoom 19. Marked uncertain.
fieldNotes.dropYard: Dedicated trailer parking area on SW dock apron (between west warehouse and main complex) with trailers parked without tractors. Functions as drop yard.
fieldNotes.multiStep: No second checkpoint resolved after the gate — single-stage entry only.
fieldNotes.rail: No rail spur into property. Major rail yard exists ~500m east beyond treeline but no spur connection visible to Kraft Heinz parcel.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter ~445m N-S × ~463m E-W = ~206,000 m² = ~51 acres for the main Kraft Heinz parcel (excluding adjacent third-party buildings).
